text: Potentially morally injurious events (PMIE) are events that violate one’s deeply held moral values or beliefs, and that have the potential to create significant inner conflict and psychological distress. PMIE have been recognized as an important psychological risk factor in many high-risk occupational groups. However, no study to date has investigated how PMIE relate to the mental health of aid workers. Furthermore, little is known about the mechanisms by which PMIE might be associated with mental health indicators.
source_label: Morally injurious events among aid workers: examining the indirect effect of negative cognitions and self-care in associations with mental health indicators
